title: Stool PCR for gut infections (rotavirus, norovirus)
what: This stool test looks for viruses and germs that cause diarrhea and vomiting.
why: For sudden diarrhea and vomiting, especially in children, and for outbreaks in a family or group.
duration: collection takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: How many days the diarrhea and vomiting have lasted
If there is blood or mucus in the stool
If anyone else in the family is sick

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Get a sterile container from a pharmacy or the lab. For stool, choose one with a small spoon in the lid.

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: It is better to do the test before starting antibiotics. If you already take them, do not stop on your own. Tell your doctor.

prepare.title: Collection
prepare.text: Collect stool from a clean surface or a diaper, not from the toilet water. Do not mix in urine.

prepare.title: Delivery
prepare.text: Bring the container to the lab the same day. Ask the lab how to store it until then.

steps: Line the potty or toilet with clean plastic wrap or paper
Use the spoon in the lid to take a bit of stool, ideally with some of the liquid part
Put it in the container. Fill no more than a third
Close it tightly and label it
Wash your hands and take the container to the lab
feel: Nothing unpleasant. It is a normal stool sample
Collecting it does not bother a child. You can take it from a potty or diaper
after: Give fluids often, in small sips. This matters most with diarrhea
Wash your hands after the toilet and after changing diapers
Your doctor will explain the result
red_flags: The child has not peed for a long time, has a dry mouth, or cries without tears: see a doctor urgently
Blood in the stool or a high fever: see a doctor the same day
Severe drowsiness, the child will not wake up, or seizures: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I collect stool from a diaper?
faq.a: Yes, if it has not soaked in. Scoop it from the surface of the diaper with the spoon.
Usually not. It is a virus. Drinking fluids is the main thing. Your doctor will prescribe treatment.

reminders.text: Stool PCR tomorrow. Get the container and clean plastic wrap ready for collection.
